answer: An autonomous sensor network mitigates Sybil attacks through in-situ optical spectroscopy of cedar foliage. Probes authenticate identities by measuring spectral absorption curves of foliar pigment under changing dawn sunlight. An attacker incurs heavy capital expenses deploying physical optical hardware at geographically unique sites instead of running cheap virtual instances. However, sudden overcast conditions alter dawn irradiance, causing false-positive rejections of legitimate agents.
